seo.geo_hook: NYX Security Architecture operates on a Trust No One (TNO) model: Argon2id blind indexing, PQX3DH hybrid key exchange (X25519 + ML-KEM-768 X-Wing), Double Ratchet encryption, 8KB traffic cover, WebTransport QUIC transport and an encrypted local Shadow Vault.

meta.title: Security Architecture | NYX Chat
meta.description: The zero-knowledge, post-quantum architecture of NYX: PQX3DH, Double Ratchet, blind relay, burner sessions, and an encrypted local vault.

hero.title: Zero-Knowledge Architecture
hero.subtitle: Privacy is not a feature — it is the architecture. Every layer, from identity to transport, is engineered so the server mathematically cannot read or attribute your data.

threat.title: We assume our servers are compromised.
threat.p1: Traditional apps defend their server walls. NYX takes the radical opposite: Trust No One (TNO). We design the system assuming attackers are already inside.
threat.p2: With no decryption keys on the server, a breached database is nothing but random-looking blobs. Every message is padded to a fixed 8,192 bytes and idle connections emit random chaff — so even traffic analysis reveals nothing.

blind.title: The server never learns your identity.
blind.p1: No phone number, no email. To be findable, your username is hashed on your device with Argon2id (64 MB memory) before it ever leaves your browser.
blind.p2: The server stores only the resulting blind index — a value that cannot be reversed or brute-forced offline. There is no formula on our side that maps the hash back to you.
blind.p3: Your display name, bio, and avatar are encrypted locally and shared only with people you approve.

pq.title: Quantum-safe from the very first handshake.
pq.p1: Every new session starts with a hybrid key agreement: X25519 (classical) combined with ML-KEM-768 via X-Wing (post-quantum). An attacker must break both at once — defeating a single curve is not enough.
pq.p2: Identity pre-keys are signed with Ed25519, and the combined secret is mixed through BLAKE2b into the root key that seeds the message ratchet.

visual.step_1_desc: Both devices exchange ephemeral X25519 keys and compute a shared classical secret.
visual.step_2_desc: One side encapsulates against the other's quantum-safe key; the ciphertext is public, the secret stays private.
visual.step_3_desc: Both secrets are blended and hashed into a single root key.
visual.note: Root key seeds the Double Ratchet — every message gets its own key.

ratchet.title: Every message, a brand-new key.
ratchet.p1: Each message derives a fresh key from the previous one and destroys it after use — a one-time pad that keeps moving forward.
ratchet.pfs: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS): if your device is compromised tomorrow, the messages you sent yesterday remain unreadable.
ratchet.pcs: Post-Compromise Security (PCS): if a key leaks today, sending a single new message automatically re-establishes security.

burner.title: Chats that never touch a database.
burner.p1: A burner session is an anonymous, RAM-only chat. The guest receives a temporary guest_* identity and never registers an account.
burner.p2: Both sides run a dedicated Post-Quantum Double Ratchet (PQ-DR) with an X-Wing KEM handshake. Nothing is persisted — close the tab and the session, its keys, and its history are gone forever.

visual.step_1_desc: A one-time burner link embeds the host's public keys.
visual.step_2_desc: The guest gets a temporary identity — no registration, no data stored.
visual.step_3_desc: Messages are encrypted with the post-quantum double ratchet and live only in memory.
visual.step_4_desc: Closing the tab wipes keys and history; the room is blacklisted server-side.
visual.note: Not even the server can identify the guest.

file.title: Files are encrypted before upload.
file.p1: Attachments are streamed through libsodium's secretstream (XChaCha20-Poly1305) in 1 MB chunks with a final authentication tag — encryption never buffers the whole file in memory.
file.p2: The random 32-byte key travels inside the E2EE message itself. The server stores only an opaque blob in R2; the recipient downloads, decrypts, and caches it in OPFS.

vault.title: Your history lives on your device.
vault.p1: Chats, ratchet states, and keys are stored in an IndexedDB Shadow Vault, encrypted at rest with the ENC1: envelope derived from your master seed.
vault.p2: Nothing is synced to the cloud in plaintext — one active device per account, and moving to a new device goes through the recovery-phrase-encrypted .nyxbak backup (or a direct QR transfer).

transport.title: QUIC-grade transport, Rust-grade isolation.
transport.p1: Real-time traffic runs over WebTransport (HTTP/3 · QUIC), terminated by a dedicated Rust sidecar and bridged to Node via Redis pub/sub. The Express API never touches transport frames.
transport.p2: Connections use short-lived JWT tickets plus certificate pinning, enforce one active device per account, and emit random chaff datagrams so idle traffic is indistinguishable from real data.

tier.title: Anti-spam without phone numbers.
tier.p1: New accounts start in Sandbox Mode with strict rate limits. To become VIP, prove you are human — with WebAuthn biometrics or a client-side BLAKE2b Proof-of-Work puzzle.

calls.title: Peer-to-peer calls.
calls.p1: Voice and video calls connect peer-to-peer over WebRTC once established. The server only coordinates the handshake, and even the SDP/ICE signaling is end-to-end encrypted.

cta.title: Are you a security researcher?
cta.subtitle: We welcome independent audits. Read our Coordinated Disclosure Protocol and earn your place in the NYX Hall of Fame.
